author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Brown University welcomed more than 3,200 new undergraduate, graduate and medical students to Providence for the 2026-27 academic year. A week of orientation activities began September 2 and culminated in the university's 263rd Opening Convocation on September 8, with fall classes beginning afterward.

The schedule mixed practical introductions with campus traditions. New students attended resource fairs and tours, learned about Brown's Open Curriculum and took part in dance events, games and informal music sessions. The program was designed to help students find academic support, understand university expectations and begin building connections before coursework accelerated.

The arriving group adds thousands of new residents to College Hill and the broader Providence community at the start of the fall term. Events also introduced students to the city, including WaterFire and other local activities. Brown's first-week program spans several schools and degree levels, so the shared ceremonies provide one of the few moments when the incoming undergraduate, graduate and medical cohorts begin the year together.
dek: Orientation events in Providence led into Brown's 263rd Opening Convocation and the start of fall classes.
headline: Brown welcomes more than 3,200 new students for 2026-27
